newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda to expand in UK, build new Europe plant-paper.
newsitem.headline: Honda to expand in UK, build new Europe plant-paper.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd plans to boost its output in Europe early next century to between 300,000 and 400,000 cars by investing about 60 billion yen in its existing plant in Britain and building a new plant in elsewhere in Europe, a Japanese newspaper said on Wednesday.
The carmaker is currently capable of producing 100,000 cars a year at its British plant, the business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
It said Honda was planning to build its second plant in Europe outside of Britain as early as 2001 to make 100,000 to 200,000 small passenger cars a year.
Honda will also invest about 60 billion yen in its British plant, currently its only plant in Europe, to increase its production capacity to 150,000 cars a year by the end of 1998, the paper said.
It said Toyota Motor Corp was also considering building a new plant in continental Europe in 2001.
Neither Honda nor Toyota were immediately available for comment on the report.
Countries Honda is considering as a possible site for its second European plant include France, Germany and Spain, the paper said.

Countries from which Toyota is likely to select the site for its new plant include France and eastern European countries such as Poland, the paper said. Toyota is expected to decide the site in early 1998, it said.
If Toyota decides to build the plant in France, it may consider a tie-up with Peugeot SA and Renault SA, the paper said.

Toyota and Honda are planning to boost their output in Europe in view of an expected increase in sales of cars in the European Union, which is expected to include eastern European nations in the future, the paper said.
